messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] reading/opening .fst files
parts:
You need to say more about what the files are and what you're trying to do.
The fst package is for reading/writing fst files.

The qtl2fst package (https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2fst) uses the fst package to store genotype probabilities in this format on disk.

karl

messages.subject: Fwd: reading/opening .fst files
parts:
I want to calculate the parent's contribution to a MAGIC population.

I run the following code:
cc <- read_cross2("Path to MAGIC.json_updated.zip")

pr <- calc_genoprob(cc, error_prob=0.002)


tmpdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "cc_genoprob")
dir.create(tmpdir)
fpr <- fst_genoprob(pr, "pr", tmpdir)


apr <- genoprob_to_alleleprob(pr)
fapr <- fst_genoprob(apr, "apr", tmpdir)

af_ind <- calc_geno_freq(apr, "individual")
par(mfrow=c(4,2))
for(i in 1:8) hist(af_ind[,i], main=colnames(af_ind)[i], breaks=30)



strains <- c("parent1", "parent2", "parent3", "parent4", "parent5", "parent6", "parent7",  "parent8")


# plots of allele frequencies across the genome
af_mar <- calc_geno_freq(apr, "marker", omit_x=FALSE)


plot_coefCC(af_mar, cc$pmap, ylim=c(0, max(af_mar)), ylab="Allele frequency", legend="topleft", legend_lab=strains)


I get all the apr.fst and pr.fst and two separately for each chromosome, and I get apr_fstindex.rds and pr_fstindex.rds (in storage)

I can see plots are generated but would like to be able to extract and write each of those .fst files as a table in txt. 

Thanks

I would start with the apr and pr objects, but there is not really an easy way to save these to a plain text file, as they consist of a set of three-dimensional arrays.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Fwd: reading/opening .fst files
parts:
Thank you Karl. I just used fst package and I was able to generate a table for each chromosome as text:
install.packages("fst")
library(fst)
library(data.table)
mydf <- read.fst("path to apr_1.fst")
write.table(mydf,"path to output\\apr_1.txt", sep="\t", quote=F)

Thank you
Atena
